question.text: In response to the famine, the UK repealed these laws, which imposed tariffs on imported grains, not a vegetable with yellow kernels as the name would suggest.
question.clue: David Ricardo published a treatise blaming them for the decrease in stock market profits.

swap.text: The Normans were led at Hastings by this man, who became King of England afterwards and commissioned the Domesday Book.
swap.answerHtml: William the Conqueror [or William I; or William the Bastard; or William II of Normandy; accept Guillaume in place of William; prompt on William]
swap.clue: This man's greatest victory is depicted on the Bayoux Tapestry and was preceded by the Battle of Stamford Bridge.

question.text: This English king opposed Cromwell during the Civil War. He was later executed.
question.clue: This ruler was depicted "at the hunt" by his court painter, Anthony van Dyck.

swap.leadin: Name these Prime Ministers of the United Kingdom.
swap.text: This Prime Minister of the UK leads a coalition government with Liberal Democrat Nick Clegg. At 43, he's the youngest Prime Minister in about 200 years.
swap.clue: In August 2011, this leader controversially proposed that social media might be restricted during riots, such as the ones which swept his capital earlier that month.

question.text: The Jacobites became active after this event, in which James II was overthrown due to his Catholic sympathies. The English Bill of Rights was adopted in the wake of this event.
question.clue: The losing side in this conflict was later defeated in the Battle of the Boyne during the First Jacobite Rising.

swap.text: This British explorer circumnavigated the globe successfully on both of his first two voyages before dying in Hawaii on his third. This man's ship, the HMS Endeavour, ran aground on the Great Barrier Reef in 1770.
swap.clue: This man was awarded the Copley medal for his work on preventing scurvy, and was accompanied by Joseph Banks on a voyage where he observed the transit of Venus on Tahiti.

question.leadin: Identify these European leaders of various kinds.
question.text: This king of England had Thomas a Becket murdered, and for that he was excommunicated. He was married to Isabelle of Aquitaine, and his children included the squabbler John Lackland.
question.clue: This man became king after the Treaty of Wallingford, which was signed by Empress Matilda, his mother.

swap.leadin: At a crucial point in this battle, Sir William Stanley decided to support the eventual winner.
swap.text: Name this battle fought near Ambion Hill. The Earl of Northumberland's failure to lead his troops into this battle contributed to its outcome.
swap.clue: The leader of the losing army managed to unhorse John Cheyne and kill Sir William Brandon, but failed to receive assistance from Henry Percy's reserves.

question.leadin: After being shipwrecked, this king was temporarily imprisoned by Guy I of Ponthieu.
question.text: Identify this brother of Leofwine, Gyrth and Tostig, the last of whom he eventually fought in battle.
question.clue: One rebellion against this man was joined by his brother Tostig, and he died on Senlac Hill after earlier defeating the Norwegian Harald Hardrada at the Battle of Stamford Bridge.

swap.leadin: This group's name comes from a Dutch word for "mumbler", and it included Nicholas of Hereford.
swap.text: Name these followers of John Wycliffe, a dissenting religious movement in pre-Anglican England.
swap.clue: They launched a short-lived open rebellion after William Fisher helped organize them at St. Giles Fields, which would have been led by a man who inspired the depiction of Falstaff, John Oldcastle.

question.text: This man, who served as PM under George III, resigned following Cornwallis's surrender at Yorktown.
question.clue: During this man's ministry, John Wilkes led troops against the Gordon Riots.

swap.leadin: The Norman English adopted this weapon after it was used against them by the Welsh in the 11th century.
swap.text: What weapon was able to fire arrows up to 100 yards with accuracy?
swap.clue: This weapon, most commonly made of yew, does not recurve and reaches from the ground to the height of its user.

question.text: The first English Bible to be printed was the Great Bible supervised by this sometime bishop of Exeter, who frequently found himself exiled from England due to his Puritanism.

swap.text: The Dutch Disaster Year followed the outbreak of war with both France and this country. The Raid on the Medway was a battle between the Dutch Republic and this polity.
swap.clue: In the mid-14th century, this kingdom's Company of the Staple was granted a monopoly on the trade of its primary export.

question.leadin: This term was coined in a 1946 speech by Winston Churchill and some commentators claimed it took a hit when Barack Obama gave Gordon Brown an unremarkable gift of DVDs.
question.text: Name this term used to describe the close ties between the UK and the United States following World War II.
question.clue: This two-word phrase describing the U.S. and United Kingdom's bromance. It was coined by Winston Churchill during his "Sinews of Peace" Address in Fulton, Missouri.

swap.leadin: It was originally organized as the anti-federalist party, and the whip of this party was withdrawn from Godfrey Bloom after he attacked a journalist in the street.
swap.text: Name this far-right political party in the UK led by Nigel Farange.

question.text: On the recapture of South Georgia, Margaret Thatcher jingoistically told reporters to "congratulate our armed forces and the Marines" and to do this action. Ted Heath is said to have sardonically repeated this word after Thatcher resigned.
question.answerHtml: “rejoice” [or word forms such as rejoicing; accept “just rejoice at that news and congratulate our forces and the Marines”; accept “rejoice, rejoice”; accept “rejoice, rejoice, rejoice”]

swap.leadin: It originated in 1295 AD, when an agreement at Dunfermline Abbey cemented a marriage between Edward Balliol and Jeanne de Valois.
swap.text: Name this military union between France and Scotland, which lasted for several centuries and was meant to control En-glish expansion.
swap.clue: The marriage of Mary of Scotland and Francis caused the temporary revival of this alliance, which ceased to be after Francis's death and the loss of all the King of England's claims in France.

question.text: Owen the Bald was a ruler of this Celtic kingdom of southern Scotland and northern England that had its capital at Dumbarton Rock.
question.answerHtml: Strathclyde [or Srath Chluaidh; or Strath of the Clyde; or Alt Clut]

swap.text: Erasmus Darwin co-founded this Enlightenment intellectual club in Birmingham whose members included Joseph Priestly and Josiah Wedgewood. Its members were punningly called "lunaticks."
